claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level (or none) misplaces the clause in the outline that page_workunit, citation and section lookups read, so the clause is attributed to the wrong parent or not found as a section.
claim.note: Heading at the wrong level: the transcription's convention is one '#' per numbering component (7. is '#', 7.1 '##', 6.4.1 '###', 6.4.2.1 '####', 6.4.2.1.1 '#####'); its sibling 6.4.2.1.1 is '#####' on page 183, so this should be '#####'.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (folio IV-38) shows '6.4.2.1.2 Definition of Conditional Sentence' as a numbered subclause heading. The transcription renders it '#### 6.4.2.1.2', the same level as its parent '#### 6.4.2.1 Conditional Statements and Sentences' (page 183), while its sibling '##### 6.4.2.1.1' (page 183) is level 5. The file's convention in this clause is one '#' per numbering component (## 6.4, ### 6.4.1, #### 6.4.1.1, ##### 6.4.1.4.1), so 6.4.2.1.2 should be '#####'. As written, an outline reader makes it a sibling of 6.4.2.1 rather than its child. The heading text is correct; only the level is wrong.
verdict.corrected_description: The heading is present but one level too shallow: '#### 6.4.2.1.2' should be '##### 6.4.2.1.2' (wrong level, not missing). The same page has the same one-level drift for its siblings: '### 6.4.2.2' should be '####', and '#### 6.4.2.2.1' and '#### 6.4.2.2.2' should be '#####'. The same is true of '### 6.4.2.3' and '#### 6.4.2.3.1' on page 185.
